reports.title: Aflac Incorporated Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results,

lines: Aflac Japan's underlying earned premiums1 – which excludes the impact of reinsurance, paid-up policies and deferred profit liability – declined 1.2%, roughly in line with where we expect to be for the full year.

Recognizing that the year-to-date benefit ratio is 58.8%, we now expect for 2026 that the benefit ratio in Japan will be slightly below the 60% to 63% range, and we expect the expense ratio to be on the lower end of the 20% to 23% range.

In the U.S., we expect the benefit ratio for 2026 to be below the 48% to 52% range and the expense ratio to be in the middle of the 36% to 39% range as we continue to scale network dental and group life and disability.
At the same time, we expect pretax profit margin for 2026 in the U.S. to be above the 17% to 20% range.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS down 2% to $2.43, well above estimates; investment losses cut net profit to $303m
results: Adjusted EPS slipped 2% to $2.43 (a weaker yen cost 3 cents), but $453m of reserve remeasurement gains helped keep it far above the $1.80 estimate.
Net profit fell to $303m from $1.6bn, mainly on $1.1bn of investment losses from repositioning the bond portfolio, plus a $51m tax charge.
Japan: pretax adjusted earnings fell 15% in yen to ¥152.3bn on higher benefits; new sales fell 4% to ¥18.8bn against a strong year-ago cancer product launch.
U.S.: premiums rose 3.3%, sales 3.5% to $403m and pretax adjusted earnings 31.5% to $493m, lifting the margin to 27.7% from 21.7%.
Aflac returned $1.1bn to shareholders and kept its Q4 dividend at $0.61, marking 44 straight years of increases.

guidance.summary: Aflac gives no earnings forecast, but set out where it expects 2026 ratios to land against its usual ranges: Japan's benefit ratio slightly below range and costs at the low end; the U.S. margin above range.

points: Japan's underlying earned premiums fell 1.2%, which management said is roughly where it expects the full year to land.
The CFO said Aflac Japan has plenty of room to cede more reserves to its Bermuda reinsurer, with an internal ceiling of about 30%, though deals may come unevenly.
Organic growth in the U.S. and Japan was named the best use of capital; third-party reinsurance remains a selective option.
U.S. growth is coming from network dental, group life and disability, which management is still scaling up.
Management sounded careful about growing capital-heavy savings products in Japan.
call.source: Prepared remarks (8-K Exhibit 99.3, outlook section) and StockStory, 6 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Japan sales return to growth once the strong 2025 cancer launch drops out of the comparison.
